findings.item: DERIVED STAT: capex intensity, FCF margin, D&A/revenue, FY2015-FY2025
findings.source_name: Derived from TSMC 4Q15-4Q25 Quarterly Management Reports
findings.note: Inputs are from the FY rows. NT$ cash-flow capex divided by US$ capex roughly equals the average FX rate each year (FY25 1,272.41/40.90 = 31.11, which is the reported average rate; FY23 31.19; FY24 32.12). This suggests US$ capex is cash-flow capex converted at average FX. Every year's FCF equals CFO minus NT$ capex exactly.

synthesis:
FACTS (TSMC 4Q management reports, 20-F, 3Q26 statements): From FY15 to FY25, USD revenue rose from US$26.61bn to US$122.42bn. Annual USD growth ranged from -8.7% (FY23) to +35.9% (FY25), with weak years in FY18 (+6.5%) and FY19 (+1.3%). OPM ranged from 34.8% (FY19) to 50.8% (FY25), and GM from 46.0% to 59.9%. Capex rose from US$8.12bn to US$40.90bn. TSMC-defined FCF ranged from NT$154.7bn (FY19) to NT$1,002.6bn (FY25). At 30-Sep-26, interest-bearing debt was NT$1,031.58bn (current portion NT$213.20bn), net cash NT$2,985.40bn and NCI NT$45.3bn. At 30-Jun-26, leases were NT$36.9bn and customer temporary receipts NT$234.2bn (Dec-25: NT$189.9bn; Dec-24: NT$291.1bn). TSMC's own FY25 USD revenue is US$122.42bn, not the ~US$122.0bn in the established list.

DERIVED: Mean USD growth was 16.4% (sample SD 15.2pp). OPM averaged 41.9% (SD 5.0pp) and GM 52.6% (SD 4.5pp). USD revenue CAGR was 16.5% for FY15-25 and 23.4% for FY19-25. Capex/revenue ranged 30.5-52.9% (mean 38.3%); FCF margin ranged 13.5-32.3% (mean 23.1%).

INFERENCE for valuation:
(1) The 3Q26 OPM of 58.7% and GM of 66.4% sit about 3.3 and 3.0 sample SDs above their 11-year means, and above the 56%+ through-cycle GM target. A terminal margin anchored on the current run-rate assumes a regime shift that history does not yet support, especially with the guided 2-4pts of overseas-fab dilution.
(2) Growth volatility is high (~15pp SD, a down year in FY23 and a near-stall in FY19). That argues for wide scenario bands even if the ~25% 2024-29 CAGR target is met on average.
(3) FCF margins compressed when capex intensity spiked (FY19, FY21, FY23). 2026 capex YTD is US$40.64bn against a US$60-64bn guide, which implies US$19.4-23.4bn in 4Q26.
(4) EV bridge: net cash is about NT$115/share (2,985.40bn / 25,932m shares). Customer temporary receipts are capacity prepayments that are later refunded or offset against receivables, so treat them as quasi-debt or operating liabilities, not free cash. Leases and NCI are each under 1% of equity.

synthesis:
FACT: On 2026-10-30 USD/TWD closed at 32.478 (CBC/Taipei Forex), the US 10Y CMT at 4.94% (Treasury; FRED's latest print was 4.98% for 10/29) and Taiwan's 10Y at ~1.99% (cnyes, Trading Economics), after the Oct-20 10Y auction cleared at 1.958% (CBC). The CBC has not hiked in 2026: rediscount rate 2.00%, unchanged since March 2024, but the Sep-17 hold passed 13-2 with two hawkish dissents; next meeting Dec 17. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September and held on Oct 28 with two dissents for a hike. Damodaran: implied US ERP 4.20% on Oct 1 (rf 5.29%); July-2026 Taiwan CRP 0.742% (total ERP 4.942%) vs 0.78%/5.01% in January. TSM ADR beta: 1.24 (5Y monthly; Yahoo, StockAnalysis), 1.31 (1Y, TradingView), 1.37 (MarketBeat). Local-share beta: 1.03 (MoneyDJ), 0.95 (1Y, TradingView); Yahoo's 2330.TW 1.24 duplicates the ADR value and is not a documented TAIEX beta. Bloomberg-compiled ADR premium averages: ~19% (4Q24), 17% (Apr-25), 24% (Jul-25), ~26% (Dec-25), 17% (Apr-26), 13.7% (May-26); 2026 daily prints ran 7.4% (Sep 1) to 18.0% (Jun 2); 16.4% on Oct 29 and ~11.3% on Oct 30. Decade/five-year averages are cited at 7.4-10%. TIKR (via Yahoo, Oct 28) shows ~17x NTM P/E vs a 5-yr average of 18x and a 25x peak (Jul-2024); TWSE trailing P/E spanned 12.5x-35.5x over 2019-2026.

INFERENCE (mine): A USD CAPM (rf 4.94%, beta 1.24-1.37, ERP 4.20-4.42% plus CRP 0.74%) gives ~10-12% cost of equity; a TWD CAPM (rf ~2.0%, beta ~1.0, ERP 4.94%) gives ~7%. The gap is mostly the ~2.95pp rate differential and should be bridged via inflation/FX, not mixed across frames. ADR betas and multiples embed a premium that compressed sharply in 2026, so value the local line and translate. At NT$2,370, FactSet consensus implies ~21.7x 2026E, ~16.3x 2027E and ~17x NTM EPS - at or slightly below the 5-yr forward average, i.e., no premium-to-history multiple is being paid.

synthesis:
FACT (2026-10-30 closes): MarketScreener consensus puts 2330 at 21.5x 2026E / 16.0x 2027E P/E and 10.1x 2027E EV/EBITDA; StockAnalysis shows the TSM ADR at 19.1x forward after its -5.95% move. Same-date next-year P/Es: NVDA 13.0x (FY Jan-28), AVGO 19.8x (FY Oct-27, GAAP basis; 16.7x non-GAAP, derived), ASML 25x, AMD 36.9x, INTC 46.5x, GFS 19.4x, UMC 15.8x, SMIC 25.1x, Samsung 3.0x, SK hynix 2.7x. Next-FY consensus revenue growth: AMD +75%, NVDA +68%, AVGO +64%, SK hynix +58%, Samsung +40%, TSMC +38% (NT$), ASML +29%, UMC +23%, SMIC +19%, GFS +13%, INTC +12-14%. TTM operating margin: TSMC 58% vs SK hynix 75%, NVDA 65%, AVGO 49% (GAAP), Samsung 46%, ASML 39%, UMC 21%, AMD 16%, GFS 12%, INTC 10%, SMIC 9%. FactSet S&P 500 forward P/E: 18.7 (Oct-29 data; 10-yr avg 19.1). Zacks (Oct-19) called TSMC's 19.8x F12M in line with the S&P 500 and its 10-yr median. Morgan Stanley (Jul-18) had it at ~17x 2027E vs a ~16.5x post-2018 average. No late-October PHLX SOX forward P/E was found; ETF aggregates were SOXX 16.75x and SMH 16.55x.
INFERENCE: (1) TSMC carries no growth premium. A derived local-share NTM P/E of ~17x is ~9% below the S&P 500 despite ~33% 2027E EPS growth. It also sits in the NVDA/AVGO band even though their consensus growth is higher, so a re-rating case must rest on lower estimate risk, not on looking cheap next to its customers. (2) Memory peers at ~3x are pricing peak-cycle earnings. Exclude them from peer medians; they also pull down the ETF aggregates. (3) Excluding memory and the trough-earnings AMD/INTC, next-year P/Es cluster at ~13-25x, bracketing TSMC's 16x. (4) The Asian Oct-30 closes (2330, Samsung, SK hynix, UMC, SMIC) came after Intel's after-hours guide but before the US-session selloff (SOX -7.2%), so those multiples are likely stale-high. (5) Intel's multiples probably rest on estimates not yet cut for its Q4 guide.

synthesis:
FACT – demand: The four US hyperscalers that reported in late October 2026 all held or raised CY2026 capex guidance: MSFT ~US$170bn including finance leases, trimmed only because third-party capacity deliveries slipped; GOOGL US$195-205bn; AMZN ~US$220bn cash; META US$135-145bn. Simple addition gives roughly US$720-740bn, though each company defines capex differently. All four pointed to more spending in 2027: 'increase significantly', 'meaningfully more', acceleration in Microsoft's Jan-Jun 2027 half, 'continue investing aggressively'. Backlogs are very large (MSFT RPO US$677bn, AWS US$578bn, Google Cloud US$561bn, Oracle RPO US$664bn), and MSFT, GOOGL and ORCL say demand exceeds supply. Upstream, NVIDIA guides FY28 revenue to grow about 70% and calls it 'supply-constrained'. Broadcom has secured supply for ~US$115bn of FY27 AI revenue, and AMD expects data-centre revenue to more than double in 2027. TSMC says demand is 'still far above our capability today to supply', with back-end packaging short. Sell-side estimates for end-2027 CoWoS capacity range from about 170k to 280k wpm, against about 115-140k at end-2026.

FACT – financing: Capex now exceeds operating cash flow at Alphabet (Q3 FCF -US$9.1bn), Meta (-US$2.1bn) and Amazon (TTM -US$42.4bn). Funding is moving to record capital-markets issuance: Alphabet's US$84.75bn equity program, Meta's ~US$97.5bn equity plan and Microsoft's US$25bn bond. It is also moving to vendor-backed structures: NVIDIA's US$105bn SB Energy guarantee and US$279bn of supply commitments, Broadcom's residual-value support on the US$63bn Anthropic SPV, and NVIDIA/AMD/Broadcom anchoring Meta's equity raise. Oracle says its capex peaks in FY27-28. Goldman expects hyperscaler capex growth to slow to 54% in 2027 and 12% in 2028.

INFERENCE for TSMC: 2027 revenue looks limited by TSMC's own capacity rather than by demand, so near-term volume risk is low and reported price rises (CoWoS up to +20%, wafers +3-6%) are supportive. The valuation swing factor is how long demand lasts after 2028. End-demand increasingly depends on capital-market access and circular vendor financing, and that is what the October sell-off priced, not any change in TSMC's 2026-27 fundamentals. Wei's own 'probably 2029, 2030... whether in between there's a dip or not, I'm not very sure' argues for modelling a 2028-29 digestion scenario rather than a smooth fade.

synthesis:
FACT. TSMC's peak-to-trough quarterly revenue declines were -51.1% (4Q00 to 2Q01, NT$), -57.5% (3Q08 to 1Q09, NT$), -24.5% (4Q18 to 1Q19) and -22.5% (3Q22 to 2Q23, US$). Each trough came 1-3 quarters after the peak.

Trough GM/OPM:
- 2Q01: 19.0%/1.1%, at 44% utilization.
- 1Q09: 18.9%/3.1%. The original guidance had been GM 1-5% and OPM -19% to -15%.
- 1Q19: 41.3%/29.4%.
- 4Q23: 53.0%/41.6%. This margin trough lagged the revenue trough by two quarters because of N3 dilution.

Revenue regained the prior peak 9, 5, 2 and 4 quarters after the trough. Margins in the 2023 cycle needed 8 quarters (to 4Q25).

WSTS/SIA annual declines were -32% (2001), -9% (2009), -12.1% (2019; memory -32.6%, non-memory -1.7%) and -8.2% (2023). TSMC's full-year changes were -24.3%, -11.2%, +3.7% and -4.5% in NT$ (-8.7% in US$).

After the 2000 capex boom:
- Equipment sales fell 41% and then 30% (about -59% over two years); 3Q01 was down 55.6% YoY.
- TSMC cut its 2001 capex plan by about 42% within three months.
- UMC revenue fell 38.6%.
- North American carrier capex fell about 28% in 2001 and about 42% by 2002F.
- Lucent revenue fell 71% over FY00-FY03.

2026 commentary mostly projects slower growth rather than outright decline:
- Allianz: 51%, 13%, about 5% (2026-28).
- UBS (via Reuters): 76%, 25%, 6%.
- DoubleLine: 84.7%, 27.5%, 7.4%.
- Goldman says consensus implies +22% in 2027.

Wells Fargo (2027 peak), the BIS ('protracted investment bust') and Jefferies are bearish but give no decline magnitudes. The bulls (GS, BofA, Barclays O'Malley) put 2027 capex at about US$1.1-1.4tn.

INFERENCE. If capex merely plateaus, the 2019/2023 template fits: about -20% to -25% peak-to-trough quarterly revenue, GM down 6-10pp, recovery in 2-4 quarters. The 2001/2009 template (about -50%, GM down about 28pp, utilization under 50%) needs an absolute capex collapse like the 2001 telecom and equipment bust; treat it as a tail case. Memory is about 53% of the 2026 WSTS market and about 80% of its growth, so headline industry declines would overstate TSMC's drawdown. However, TSMC's heavier fixed-cost base (rising depreciation, overseas fabs, N2 ramp) probably means a larger margin loss per point of revenue decline than in 2019/2023.
